profile.summary: Evo is a 7-billion-parameter DNA language model trained on prokaryotic whole genomes. It reads DNA one base at a time, with a context of 8,192 or 131,072 bases depending on the checkpoint, and predicts the next base. The developers use it to score how likely a sequence is and to generate new DNA, from single genes and CRISPR-Cas systems up to genome-scale sequences.

summary_quotes.text: Evo has 7 billion parameters and is trained on [OpenGenome](https://huggingface.co/datasets/LongSafari/open-genome), a prokaryotic whole-genome dataset containing ~300 billion tokens.
to enable modeling of sequences at a single-nucleotide, byte-level resolution
We also provide an [example script](scripts/score.py) for using the model to score the log-likelihoods of a set of sequences.
We use this model to reason about and generate sequences at the genome scale.
A model finetuned using `evo-1-8k-base` as the base model to generate CRISPR-Cas systems.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Evo uses the StripedHyena architecture, a hybrid of multi-head attention and gated convolutions arranged in Hyena blocks. Hyena layers do most of the sequence processing and attention layers add targeted pattern recall, which gives near-linear scaling of compute and memory with context length. Tokens are single nucleotides (byte-level). The model is autoregressive: it outputs logits over the vocabulary at each position, which are used to sample new sequence or to score the log-likelihood of an existing one. Generation can run in a recurrent mode; the model card reports more than 500k bases generated on a single 80GB GPU.

quotes.text: StripedHyena is a deep signal processing, hybrid architecture composed of multi-head attention and gated convolutions arranged in [Hyena](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.10866) blocks
with Hyena layers implementing the bulk of the computation required for sequence processing and attention layers supplementing the ability to perform targeted pattern recall
with near-linear scaling of compute and memory relative to context length
**Efficient autoregressive generation** via a recurrent mode (>500k generation with a single 80GB GPU)

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: evo-1-8k-base was pretrained at 8,192 context. evo-1-131k-base continues from it at 131,072 context. Evo 1.5 (evo-1.5-8k-base) extends the pretraining of evo-1-8k-base with 50% more data, to 450 billion tokens, and was introduced in a 2025 Nature paper. Two fine-tuned models generate CRISPR-Cas systems and IS200/IS605 transposons. The model card adds 15 intermediate pretraining checkpoints as branches. The Hugging Face weights had a projection-permutation bug that affects generation; the fix is loaded with revision="1.1_fix". The evo-model package had an inference bug in versions installed between Nov 15 and Dec 16, 2024, fixed from release 0.3. A result should name the checkpoint, the Hugging Face revision and the package version. The developers now point to Evo 2 as the successor.

We have developed a new model called Evo 2 that extends the Evo 1 model and its ideas to all domains of life.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Autoregressive (next-base) DNA language model for scoring and generating sequence.

quotes.text: Evo is a biological foundation model capable of long-context modeling and design.
We provide an [example script](scripts/generate.py) for how to prompt the model and sample a set of sequences given the prompt.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: StripedHyena: hybrid of multi-head attention and gated convolutions in Hyena blocks. Mixed precision; the card asks to keep poles and residues in float32.

quotes.text: hybrid architecture composed of multi-head attention and gated convolutions
StripedHyena is a mixed precision model. Make sure to keep your `poles` and `residues` in `float32` precision

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: DNA sequence as single-nucleotide, byte-level tokens; for generation, a DNA prompt.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Logits of shape (batch, length, vocab); sampled sequences from the generation script; per-sequence log-likelihood scores from the scoring script, written to a TSV.

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: 7 billion, as stated by the developers. Hugging Face counts 6,452,781,248 in the safetensors files of both evo-1-131k-base and evo-1.5-8k-base.

run_guide.summary: Install FlashAttention and the Evo package from the pinned commit, then load evo-1-131k-base and print next-base logits for a short sequence.
prerequisites: conda, git and an NVIDIA GPU supported by FlashAttention-2. GPU memory needs are not stated in the sources read.
PyTorch >= 2.7.0 and < 2.8.0a0 with FlashAttention <= 2.7.4.post0; the conda-forge flash-attn install brings PyTorch with it.
Code and weights are Apache-2.0. The weights are not gated.

steps.title: Run one forward pass
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from evo import Evo
import torch

device = 'cuda:0'

evo_model = Evo('evo-1-131k-base')
model, tokenizer = evo_model.model, evo_model.tokenizer
model.to(device)
model.eval()

sequence = 'ACGT'
input_ids = torch.tensor(
    tokenizer.tokenize(sequence),
    dtype=torch.int,
).to(device).unsqueeze(0)

with torch.no_grad():
    logits, _ = model(input_ids) # (batch, length, vocab)

print('Logits: ', logits)
print('Shape (batch, length, vocab): ', logits.shape)
PY
steps.explanation: The README usage example, wrapped in a shell heredoc. It downloads evo-1-131k-base and runs it on the sequence ACGT.

outputs: The script prints the logits tensor and its shape, (batch, length, vocab).
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The example uses a 4-base sequence; use scripts.generate or scripts.score from the README for real generation or scoring.
FlashAttention may not build on all GPU architectures.
